messages:
rina: Heads-up: I toggled `profile_shard_cache` to scope=user_segment in staging and noticed ~0.3% of preview traces went to the spot-cost pool. Not expected.

omar: saw that in the routing heatmap. can you paste the flag you pushed?

rina: quick paste:
```json
{
  \"name\": \"profile_shard_cache\",
  \"scope\": \"user_segment\",
  \"cache_mode\": \"prefix_kv\",
  \"rollout\": {\"pct\": 15}
}
```

lucy: 15% should still favor latency pools per current route_policy. could the cache apply earlier and cause a route key mutation?

omar: yes — evaluator currently applies cache transforms before route-tier checks. there's a subtle ordering effect documented in #issue-ops-913. opened an incident note.

rina: exact symptom: small tail of requests had route_key truncated by cache prefixing -> matched low-cost matcher.

devops-bot: [12:03] Autoscaler: no scale activity in latency-pool-A. Deploys: none.

lucy: ops telemetry problem: rollout telemetry only records final route and flag id. we need an evaluation trace (tiny) and a hashed_segment id to repro.

omar: agree. proposal: add an enum-based trace list to telemetry proto. keep it compact (e.g. T1=segment-resolve, T2=cache-prefix, T3=route-check). hashed_segment ok for privacy.

rina: console preview needs to surface \"ordering impact\" estimates. right now preview assumes independent routing and reports 15%->latency-pool unchanged. instead show something like: \"Preview: 15% exposure; est. 0.35% diverted to cost-pool due to cache-ordering\".

lucy: for tooling, add a dryrun endpoint that accepts a pseudo-request (tenant_hash, route_key, seq_len, segment_salt) and returns decision + compact trace. console can call it to compute estimates.

omar: API sketch: POST /v1/flags/dryrun {tenant_hash, key, request:{route_key, seq_len, segment}} -> {decision: \"latency\", trace:[\"T1\",\"T2\",\"T3\"], estimated_route}.

rina: privacy: console dryrun must never log raw tenant ids. telemetry event for dryrun should include only flag id and sample_hash.

lucy: scaling note: adding eval-trace telemetry will increase events. gate it via flag field `telemetry_level` with values `basic|trace|off`. default basic. enable trace only during active rollouts and sample at 0.5%-1%. retain traces for 14 days.

omar: safety gate idea: if dryrun predicts >0.2% of the rollout exposure hitting non-latency pools for flags marked `latency_critical=true`, block the rollout and require an approval. console should show the blocking reason.

rina: implement plan: 1) proto enum trace + telemetry_level flag field; 2) dryrun endpoint backed by routing-sim service; 3) console preview uses dryrun to estimate routing delta and shows warning/blocks; 4) short-term revert the flag in staging until hooks exist.

lucy: i'll own proto + metrics. omar can stand up routing-sim job. ri na (sic) can do console wiring with mockups.

ui-bot: [12:21] Mockup posted in #product-ui: https://redwood.internal/s/figma/dryrun-preview (contains example text for blocking flow).

omar: one more debate: should trace use human strings on wire or compact enums? compact enums win for telemetry size; console will map codes to human text.

lucy: +1. also add an opt-in in console to request sampled full traces for investigation (audit only, gated by `trace` telemetry_level and admin perms).

rina: reverting staging flag now and adding a retro note. thanks team.

devops-bot: [12:27] Flag revert: `profile_shard_cache` rollout.pct=0 by rina.

omar: follow-up tasks: update docs `config-eval/ordering.md` with canonical evaluation order and examples, and add a small section to onboarding for flag authors.

lucy: adding that doc to the repo and will link it from the console preview help text.

rina: logging thread into rollout-retro. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
